headline: Bay depression may intensify into cyclone Arnab, landfall expected on India's Andhra coast
summary: A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal is forecast to strengthen into a cyclone named Arnab. It is expected to make landfall on India's Andhra Pradesh coast as a very severe cyclonic storm.
details: A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal has intensified and shows potential to develop into a cyclone. The Bangladesh Meteorological Department forecasts further strengthening, with a possible landfall on India's Andhra Pradesh coast as a very severe cyclonic storm.

If the system develops into a cyclone, it will be named Arnab, a name proposed by Bangladesh meaning 'ocean' or 'sea'. Cyclone naming is a collaborative process involving thirteen countries in the World Meteorological Organization's North Indian Ocean region.

As of Sunday noon, the deep depression was located 810km south of Chattogram Port, 730km south of Cox's Bazar Port, 850km south of Mongla Port, and 780km south of Payra Port. The system is moving northwestwards and is expected to intensify into a cyclone on Monday.

The cyclone may change direction and head towards the West Bengal–north Odisha coast before potentially crossing India's Andhra coast. The Meteorological Department reported sustained winds of up to 50km per hour near the depression's centre, with gusts reaching 60km per hour.

In response to the developing situation, Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Mongla, and Payra ports have been advised to hoist distant warning Signal No. 1. All fishing boats and trawlers in the northern Bay of Bengal are instructed to move closer to the coast and navigate with caution.
caption:
Cyclone Arnab may form in the Bay of Bengal.
Authorities have issued warnings for ports and fishing vessels.

headline_marked: 3 injured as [[tiger crosses border into Bangladesh]] near Lalmonirhat
headline: 3 injured as tiger crosses border into Bangladesh near Lalmonirhat
summary: A wild animal, believed to be a tiger, attacked three people including a woman at the Hatibandha border, sending them to Rangpur Medical College Hospital.
details: Three people, including a woman, were injured in a wild animal attack at the Hatibandha border in Lalmonirhat.
The victims, who were attacked by what they describe as a tiger that had crossed the border into Bangladesh, have been sent to Rangpur Medical College Hospital for treatment.
Local residents reported the animal's presence after the attack, causing alarm in the border region.
Authorities are monitoring the situation as the animal remains a threat to the local population.
